zh.title: 漢莎航空啟用Starlink高網速衛星網路 機隊計畫擴及850架
zh.summary: 漢莎航空首架Starlink客機首航；計畫2029年前裝設850架客機
body: 德國漢莎航空（Lufthansa）於2026年8月19日正式啟用星鏈（Starlink）衛星網路服務，首航由一架國籍註冊編號為D-AINM的空中巴士A320neo執飛，執行從法蘭克福飛往羅馬的LH234班機。該班機於當地時間中午12時15分自法蘭克福起飛，當客機升至約1,0000公尺高度時，漢莎航空執行長詹斯·里特（Jens Ritter）正式開啟機上Wi-Fi系統，完成歐洲航空業者大型機上網路升級計畫的重要里程碑。
漢莎航空表示，這架註冊號為D-AINM的A320neo客機將繼續投入定期航班營運，搭乘該航空歐洲航線網路的旅客均有機會體驗這項新服務。此外，漢莎航空集團規劃在2029年前，為旗下各航空公司約850架客機完成Starlink系統裝設。在2026年底前，預計還會有最多10架由漢莎航空及漢莎城市航空（Lufthansa City Airlines）營運的A320系列客機完成設備組裝。

機上Starlink設備的安裝作業主要安排在柏林的漢莎技術（Lufthansa Technik）基地進行，並配合預定的定期技術檢修同時實施，以減少客機停飛的時間。在服務收費方面，只要旅客使用機上Travel ID或「飛常條碼」（Miles & More）會員身分登入，即可免費使用Starlink網路服務。不論旅客搭乘的是經濟艙、商務艙或頭等艙，均享有相同的免費高速連線權限，相較於舊有FlyNet機上網路方案需要額外收費模式，提供了重大轉變。
根據漢莎航空說明，全新的Starlink高頻寬連線讓機上網路體驗更接近地面環境，旅客可進行一般網頁瀏覽、傳送訊息、線上串流影片，以及執行雲端辦公與協作文件等高頻寬需求應用，並支援同時連接多台設備。然而，為了維護客艙安靜與搭乘品質，漢莎航空目前禁止旅客在機上進行語音或視訊通話，亦不得進行直播，播放影音時則須配戴耳機。該服務同時提供閘口至目的地的全全程連線能力。

en.title: Lufthansa Launches Starlink Wi-Fi Rollout with First Passenger Flight, Targeting 850 Aircraft
en.summary: Lufthansa debuts Starlink Wi-Fi on flight LH234, planning to equip 850 aircraft by 2029.
body: German carrier Lufthansa operated its first passenger flight equipped with Starlink satellite Wi-Fi onboard on August 19, 2026, marking the official launch of its inflight connectivity upgrade program. The inaugural service was performed by an Airbus A320neo registered as D-AINM, operating flight LH234 from Frankfurt to Rome. The flight departed Frankfurt at 12:15 local time, and Lufthansa Chief Executive Officer Jens Ritter activated the system once the aircraft reached an altitude of approximately 10,000 metres.

The equipped Airbus A320neo will remain in regular scheduled service across Lufthansa's European flight network. This deployment represents the first phase of a broader initiative by Lufthansa Group, which aims to equip approximately 850 aircraft across its member airlines with Starlink high-speed internet by 2029. Before the end of 2026, the group expects to equip up to ten additional A320-family aircraft operated by Lufthansa and Lufthansa City Airlines.

Equipment installation is being conducted primarily at the Lufthansa Technik facility in Berlin, integrated with scheduled maintenance checks to minimize operational aircraft downtime. Under the new commercial offering, Starlink Wi-Fi is accessible free of charge to all passengers who sign in using a Lufthansa Group Travel ID or Miles & More membership. The free high-speed connectivity applies uniformly across all cabin classes, including Economy, Business, and First Class, departing from the carrier's legacy FlyNet pricing tier system.

Lufthansa stated that the increased bandwidth allows inflight connectivity to perform similarly to ground-based internet networks, enabling passengers to browse websites, stream videos, send messages, and access cloud-based work tools across multiple devices. However, based on passenger feedback, the airline maintains policy restrictions prohibiting voice and video calls as well as live streaming during flights to prevent cabin noise disturbance. The system provides gate-to-destination coverage throughout the entire flight duration.

zh.title: 薩里大學研究警告太空天氣對航空風險增加 呼籲建立應對標準
zh.summary: 薩里大學研究警告太空天氣風險增加，極端太陽風暴可干擾客機電子系統與通訊。
body: 由英國薩里大學（University of Surrey）學者主導並發表於《太空天氣與太空氣候期刊》（Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate）的最新研究警告，太空天氣對航空安全構成的風險，已超出目前產業應對程序的考量範圍。研究指出，當太陽釋放異常強烈的偏高能量粒子進入大氣層時，將顯著提高巡航高度（約8至14公里）的輻射水平。

研究團隊指出，高能粒子會引發半導體電子電路的「單事件翻轉」（Single Event Upsets, SEUs）或「位元翻轉」，改變電路狀態並干擾飛控電腦運作。國際民航組織（ICAO）的太空天氣手冊亦指出，半導體航空電子設備在太陽輻射事件期間可能發生故障，單事件翻轉更可能導致電腦系統重置。雖然現代客機設有容錯與備份機制，但研究估計在極端太空天氣下，單事件翻轉發生率可能從平時每小時數次暴增至數千次。
研究並列舉歷史數據說明太空氣候的威脅。在2025年11月發生的一次重大太陽風暴期間，高空輻射測量值達到正常水平的近十倍。此外，對1956年2月極端太陽事件的模擬顯示，同等強度的太陽風暴可能使乘客承受相當於正常飛行約一整年的宇宙輻射累積劑量。
國際民航組織表示，由於極地地區磁場防禦能力較弱，跨越極地與近極地的航線在太陽輻射風暴期間面臨最高風險。太空天氣同時可能干擾高頻無線電通訊，並削弱衛星導航與監視系統的性能。研究主導作者雷凡（Fan Lei）博士提到，先前發生的空中巴士A320（Airbus A320，ICAO機型代碼A320）停飛事件與宇宙輻射相關，顯示太空氣候已對航空運營產生實際影響，航空公司亟需明確的改道、降高或停飛決策標準。

en.title: University of Surrey Study Warns Space Weather Poses Growing Risk to Aviation Safety
en.summary: University of Surrey study warns space weather poses growing risks to aircraft electronics and flight safety.
body: A research study led by the University of Surrey and published in the Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate warns that space weather poses a greater risk to aviation safety than current industry procedures fully account for. The research examined the effects of powerful bursts of solar energetic particles reaching the Earth's atmosphere, causing elevated radiation levels at normal commercial cruising altitudes of 8 to 14 kilometers.

The researchers highlighted significant risks to aircraft electronics, noting that high-energy solar particles can trigger Single Event Upsets (SEUs), or "bit flips," which alter electronic circuit states. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) space weather manual confirms that semiconductor avionics can malfunction during radiation events and SEUs can force computer systems to reset. While aircraft feature fault-tolerant redundancy, the Surrey study estimates SEU rates could increase from a few per hour under normal conditions to thousands during extreme space weather.

Historical evidence underlines the potential severity of solar storms. High-altitude radiation measurements reached nearly ten times normal levels during a major solar storm in November 2025. Modeling of the powerful February 1956 solar event indicates that a storm of comparable strength could expose passengers to radiation equivalent to roughly a year's worth of typical cosmic radiation received during normal flights.

Polar and near-polar routes are particularly vulnerable during solar radiation storms because the Earth's magnetic field offers less shielding near the poles. According to ICAO, space weather events can also disrupt high-frequency radio communications and degrade satellite-based navigation and surveillance systems. Study lead author Dr. Fan Lei cited a recent Airbus A320 (ICAO type code A320) grounding linked to cosmic radiation as evidence that space weather is already affecting flight operations, calling for clearer operational thresholds for rerouting or grounding aircraft.
